subject: Re: capacity for Black Friday spike — short window rate split & approval
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@sprucecommerce.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sprucecommerce.com
Date: 2026-11-14T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity lift ask for Black Friday test run

Hi Jonas,

Quick note — we have a 48-hour stress test planned the week before Black Friday to validate caching and latency optimizations for our checkout assistant. Expected burst is ~3-4x normal traffic for two 8-hour windows on 2026-11-25. Can Redwood provide: 1) an on-demand short-window quota lift, 2) a clear overrun rate (tokens) if we exceed the uplift, and 3) a quote for a provisional committed headroom for that week?

Procurement looped in for PO timing. We need commercial clarity by COB Monday so internal ops can greenlight the test.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Director of Platform — Spruce Commerce

---
Attachment: test-plan-summary.txt (text/stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@sprucecommerce.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity lift ask for Black Friday test run

Hi Anika — great to hear the timing and thanks for the heads up. Quick summary of what we can offer for the 48-hr test:

- Temporary headroom: +300% concurrency cap for two 8-hour windows (non-recurring).
- Overrun pricing if usage exceeds the uplift: baseline paygo rate + a 40% short-window surcharge (per-1k tokens).
- Option A (short-term): One-off provisional headroom with no commit, immediate provisioning, prorated billing.
- Option B (safety-net commit): 2-week micro-commit equal to 150% of your historical weekly usage; includes a 20% discount on the short-window surcharge and priority routing.

I've attached a quick pricing-comparison workbook and a draft SOW with timing and operational runbook. If you prefer, we can propose a hybrid split: apply Option B for the primary window and Option A as a fallback for the second window to avoid over-committing.

Ben (cc'd) and Laura — can you weigh in on whether we can tighten the surcharge to 30% for this account if they sign the micro-commit and provide a PO by EOD Monday?

Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0163

---
Attachments: pricing-comparison-Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet/stub), SOW-draft-v2.pdf (pdf/stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity lift ask for Black Friday test run

Jonas — thanks. Two quick internal points:

1) We can do 30% surcharge with the micro-commit, but only if the micro-commit covers at least 120% of their average weekly consumption and is billed upfront as a credit. That protects us for the short-window delta.
2) Recommend adding an "ephemeral burst credit" clause in the SOW: up to X tokens covered for free during the first 4 hours of the primary window to reduce churn risk from unexpected throttling. That gives Spruce time to react without immediate surcharges.

If they push procurement to sign a PO by EOD Monday, I can escalate for the 30% concession. Laura — can legal accept an ephemeral credit cap and a 48-hr elevated SLA for that window (we'll need to scope SLA exceptions)?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Commercial | Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity lift ask for Black Friday test run

Ben/Jonas — legal is okay with an ephemeral burst credit but we need the cap spelled out numerically (e.g., 250M tokens) and a clear waterfall: 1) ephemeral credit, 2) micro-commit credit, 3) overrun surcharge. Also require that any PO includes the micro-commit SKU code and a billing contact.

I'll prepare a one-paragraph amendment to the SOW that includes: cap, waterfall, and the shortened signature timeline. If procurement signs PO by 2026-11-16 17:00 PT, we can commit to the 30% surcharge concession and priority capacity routing.

Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
---
Note: loop in Finance if they request invoice net terms shorter than 30 days.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@sprucecommerce.com>, procurement@sprucecommerce.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Commercial proposal: short-window micro-commit + ephemeral credit (Spruce Commerce)

Anika / Procurement team — attaching the revised SOW and a short pricing comparison. Highlights:

- Micro-commit SKU: SPR-MC-150 (150% weekly usage prepaid as credit) — priced at $12,500 (covers compute + priority routing).
- Ephemeral burst credit: 250,000,000 tokens free applied to primary 8-hr window (first 4 hours fully covered, next 4 hours covered up to cap).
- Overrun model: paygo rate $0.0035 per 1k tokens + 30% short-window surcharge if micro-commit signed by 2026-11-16 17:00 PT. Otherwise surcharge reverts to 45%.
- DocuSign link for the amendment: https://docusign.com/ABC-123-signature

If procurement can return a signed PO or the DocuSign by EOD Monday we'll provision the uplift and lock the 30% surcharge. Happy to jump on a 15-minute call to run through the SOW and timing.

Cheers,
Jonas

---
Attachments: SOW-draft-v2.pdf (with amendment paragraph), pricing-comparison-Q4.xlsx

Jonas/Ben — thanks, this looks good. Procurement approved the micro-commit and we routed the PO internally this afternoon (PO# SC-112244). We signed the DocuSign and you should see the envelope complete. Two asks before provisioning:

1) Please confirm the token accounting method (how the ephemeral credit will be consumed and reported in the console).
2) Can you confirm billing contact: finance@sprucecommerce.com and that invoice terms are Net 30?

If you confirm both, we'll consider the uplift executed on receipt of PO and DocuSign.

- Anika
